thread:
maria (oncall): Pager alert: canary-health alert firing — 5xx rate jumped to 6.8% on eu-west-1 after the 03:14 deploy. Not sure if rollback auto kicked yet.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2048 — Canary 503 spike. Trigger: canary-health >5% for 2m. Paging: maria (oncall).
kevin: I'm on it. Anyone see the rollout ID?
sophie: rollout-id: r2026-03-17-3503 (canary 2/10). Deployed model variant v2-quant-light.
josh: seeing logs: repeated L7 retries from the frontend -> 504s and 503s in the canary group, stack traces show kv-cache misses and grpc timeouts to transformer workers.
maria (oncall): infra-bot — did the automated rollback trigger?
infra-bot: Auto-rollback policy: threshold met but rollback suppressed due to "kill-switch: manual" on customer-tier in org-config. Condition: policy abort=true. (See /ops/rollouts/3503)
kevin: ah — the feature flag kill-switch for emergency rollback had "interlock: confirm" enabled. That requires a manual flip of the flag in terraform -> flag-propagation takes ~30-45s. Looks like race between autoscaler/health and flag propagation.
sophie: summary: Autosensor detected bad canary and would have rolled back, but org-level kill-switch is manual-only. propagation lag + service-mesh config caching kept traffic hitting the canary for ~3m.
josh: customer impact estimate — 1.2% of traffic affected during window, about ~73k requests, a handful of enterprise customers saw increased error rates. No data loss.
kevin: plan: 1) flip emergency flag to unwind canary traffic (manual). 2) if traffic not draining in 60s, perform manual rollback of canary to previous revision. 3) run smoke checks and validate telemetry.
maria (oncall): I'm flipping the flag now. @kevin prepare rollback command and verification steps.
kevin: executing: ```
# flip flag to allow automatic evict
redwood feature-flag set canary_kill_switch --env=prod --value=evacuate --actor=maria
# if needed rollback
redwood deploy rollback --target=r2026-03-17-3503 --to=r2026-03-16-2301 --force --reason="canary-503-spike"
```
kevin: flag flip acknowledged. propagation started.
maria (oncall): :large_green_circle: flipped. infra-bot shows propagation 0/3 -> 2/3 -> 3/3 (eu-west propagation).
josh: logs show traffic routing diverging now; 85% of canary traffic moved to baseline within 40s. 503s falling.
sophie: running smoke tests: ```
curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .status
# expect: "ok"
```
maria (oncall): smoke all good so far. Still holding on full rollback.
kevin: monitoring metrics: 5xx down to 0.9% in canary group. latency normalized. I'll hold on rollback but we should validate with synthetics and business metrics.
pm-oliver: (PM) Quick note: Incidents to customer ops — 3 customers saw elevated errors for ~4m. No order failures. We'll draft a short external blurb.
sophie: verifying post-condition: kv-cache warmup caused some requests to hit code path that assumes new embedding dimension. Those backend calls timed out. That explains 5xx. Quantized model variant exposed an unhandled edge-case if kv-cache miss + cold-start.
josh: filed issue: GH-4897 referencing the runtime guard missing for kv-miss in v2-quant-light.
kevin: marking INC-2048 as mitigated. Manual rollback not required (flag flip sufficed). Recording steps in runbook.
maria (oncall): thanks team. Follow-ups: 1) fix runtime guard GH-4897, 2) adjust feature-flag propagation docs and consider autosafe fallback to trigger immediate rollback if propagation lag > threshold, 3) customer communication draft (pm-oliver).
pm-oliver: I'll start the customer note and loop in support.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2048 updated: status=resolved, mitigated_by=feature-flag-evacuate, duration=00:07:15. Postmortem owner: kevin.
kevin: assigning postmortem, will include timeline, propagation metrics, and playbook changes. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.
maria (oncall): closing channel in 10m unless new alerts. :thumbsup:
kevin: :thumbsup: will follow up in #postmortems with action items.
